kicker: From countless grains of data sand, a “brain” slowly takes shape.

brain.label: A brain of light
brain.aria: Gather the sand into a brain
brain.help: Press and hold, or hold Space or Enter, to gather the sand into a brain; hold again to scatter it back into sand. The “Sand – Brain” slider moves back and forth. Drag or use the arrow keys to turn the brain.
brain.done: The grains have gathered into a “brain” made of threads of light.
brain.insight: AI is software doing tasks that seem to need a mind; today it mostly teaches itself from mountains of data.
brain.detail: The “brain” here is just a metaphor: AI isn’t a living brain, but software running on computers.
brain.noWebgl: Still image: grains of data sand gathering into a “brain”.

ladder.label: One task, four ways
ladder.pathLabel: Four ways a computer answers the same letter. Use the arrow keys to step from stone to stone.
question: Is Brick Red still in stock?
Will it suit darker skin?

eras.name: Traditional software
eras.insight: Traditional software only follows “if… then…” rules that people wrote in advance.

milestone.text: In the 1980s, “expert systems” — software running on many “if… then…” rules drawn from experts’ knowledge — were a popular kind of AI.

eras.name: Machine Learning
eras.insight: Machine learning: the computer studies lots of examples that come with answers, then finds the patterns itself.

milestone.text: In 1959, Arthur Samuel (IBM) published a checkers program that got better the more it played — an early work using the phrase “machine learning”.

eras.name: Deep Learning
eras.insight: Deep learning uses networks with many layers; each layer picks up a deeper level of meaning.

milestone.text: In 2012, the AlexNet network won the ImageNet image-recognition contest by a wide margin, kicking off the deep learning wave.

eras.name: Generative AI
eras.reply: Hi there! Brick Red is still in stock. On darker skin, a thin coat looks lovely.
eras.insight: Generative AI doesn’t just sort things — it creates new content, and you give the final approval.

milestone.text: In 2017, “Attention Is All You Need” introduced the Transformer — the foundation of most large language models (LLMs) behind today’s AI chatbots.

ladder.final: Over time, people write fewer rules and machines learn more from data — but a human still needs to check.
ladder.finalDetail: Generative AI can still get things wrong or make things up, so read it over before sending it to a customer.

nextWord.label: Guess the next word
nextWord.insight: AI writes by repeatedly guessing a likely next word — something it learned from huge amounts of text.
nextWord.regen: Many words fit, so AI may pick a different one — that’s why each “regenerate” usually gives you a new sentence.

quiz.q: How is machine learning different from traditional software?
quiz.explain: Machine learning finds patterns in examples on its own, instead of only following rules people wrote in advance.

summary: Today’s AI mostly learns from data; chatbots write by guessing the next word.
